tagline: From scrub oak to spruce, under the top of the Wasatch.
intro: From Payson the loop road climbs out of the valley on 600 East and Forest Road 15, through scrub oak into maple and quaking aspen and on into fir, Engelmann spruce and lodgepole pine. At the Utah Valley overlook the view funnels back down between canyons to the lake in the valley. Ahead is Mount Nebo, the southernmost and highest peak in the Wasatch.

Nebo has two summits. Early surveys called the southern one higher, and a resurvey in the 1970s gave it to the northern by about fifty feet. The road comes down at last to SR-132, five miles from I-15 at Nephi.

moments.title: Payson Lakes
moments.text: Twelve miles south of Payson, three lakes with brook and rainbow trout and a paved path around the water. The historic guard station rents as a cabin.

moments.title: Devils Kitchen
moments.text: A half-mile round trip on a paved trail to red sandstone hoodoos, a small piece of Bryce Canyon set down among the mountain greenery.

moments.title: Mount Nebo
moments.text: The overlook faces the peak. The hike to the top climbs 5,500 feet, and one old-time local rider warns there are dead horses in every canyon on the mountain.

practical: The road is closed in winter.
